requirements.title: Select Client and Access Client-Specific Clinical Functionality

acceptanceCriteria.text: The user can access the Client area. Observable outcome: the Client area is displayed.
The user can select a client from the Client selector. Observable outcome: the selected client is displayed in the Client selector.
The selected client provides the active context for Skills Programs. Observable outcome: Skills Programs displays information for the selected client.
acceptanceCriteria.coverageJustification: Held at S3 pending GAP-010. Whether showing another client's data in a read-only view is a clinical-rules.md section 21 association failure or a lesser context error decides the assertion strength, and writing the test against the wrong strength would produce a test that passes while the defect ships. Deferred deliberately, not overlooked. See aidlc-docs/design/REQ-CLIENT-001/coverage-matrix.md.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The selected client provides the active context for Analyze Data. Observable outcome: Analyze Data displays information and controls for the selected client.

clinicalRules.statement: Patient identity must be verified before acting on patient data. Applies to client selection because the ratified taxonomy holds Client and Patient to be the same entity.
Clinical data must remain associated with the correct patient/client.

testCases.objective: A user who can access the application reaches the Client area and finds it displayed with a client selector offering at least one client.
Selecting a client makes that client the active client, and demonstrably not another client offered by the same selector.

blockers.description: Is showing another client's data in a read-only view a clinical-rules.md section 21 association failure, or a lesser context error? The answer decides whether AC-003 to AC-005 assert data integrity or context correctness, and therefore the assertion strength and defect severity.

The clinical sign-off for REQ-CLIENT-001 was given by the same person who approved as QA lead. Permissible under clinical-rules.md section 5 and defensible under section 35 given a read-only workflow, but recorded rather than left implicit.
blockers.resolution: Accepted on risk grounds for this requirement. Explicitly does not carry over to REQ-CLIENT-002, which writes clinical data; an independent SME was required there on 2026-08-25.

blockers.description: Which data mode the suite may run against. The application substitutes example data when the backend does not respond, so a green run can reflect fallback data rather than real behaviour — a false pass no retry policy detects, because nothing is intermittent.
blockers.resolution: Any mode tolerated, but recorded as execution evidence. Both executions in this record ran under data-mode: substituted, captured as a Playwright annotation.

blockers.description: Expected results for this requirement derive from screenshots of the running application, which rank seventh of eight in the aidlc-e2e-rules.md section 3 source hierarchy. The approval did not characterise the requirement as a regression baseline. These tests detect change from current behaviour; they cannot detect a defect already present in it.
